hero.description: Vancouver is one of the most scenic cities in North America — and one of the most soccer-passionate. BC Place's retractable roof means rain is never an issue, and the SkyTrain drops fans two minutes from the gate. For natural beauty between matches, no World Cup city comes close.

stadium.name: BC Place
stadium.transport: BC Place sits in central Downtown Vancouver. The Stadium-Chinatown SkyTrain station (Expo and Millennium Lines) is a 2-minute walk from the main gate. SkyTrain runs extended hours on match nights — the most convenient stadium access in the tournament.

quick_facts.fan_hub_status: Major fan hub expected near BC Place and Plaza of Nations; confirm schedules

weather.june: Mild with highs around 20–22°C (68–72°F). June can be rainy — Vancouver's 'Junuary' effect. Bring a jacket.
weather.july: Best month of the Vancouver summer. Highs 22–26°C (72–79°F), lower humidity, beautiful clear days.
packing_tips: Pack a light waterproof jacket regardless of forecast — Vancouver rain is unpredictable
Layers for evening matches — temperatures drop noticeably after sunset even in July
Comfortable walking shoes — Vancouver's hills reward proper footwear
Sunscreen for beach days and outdoor fan events in July

airports.name: Vancouver International Airport
transfer_options: Canada Line SkyTrain: YVR Airport to Waterfront Station in about 26 minutes — best option
Transfer at Waterfront to Expo/Millennium Line for Stadium-Chinatown stop
Rideshare from YVR to Downtown takes 20–40 minutes depending on traffic
Taxi costs roughly $35–45 to Downtown Vancouver
airports.notes: Exceptional airport transit — the Canada Line SkyTrain goes directly from the airport terminal to Downtown. Buy a Compass Card at the airport for seamless travel throughout your stay.

match_schedule.teams_or_placeholder: BC Place hosts multiple tournament matches. Official schedule released after group draw.

public_transit: Stadium-Chinatown SkyTrain station: Expo and Millennium Lines — 2-minute walk to BC Place main gate
Canada Line connects YVR Airport to Waterfront, then Expo Line to Stadium-Chinatown
Multiple bus routes serve Pacific Blvd corridor on match days
rideshare: Rideshare pickup is practical but traffic on Pacific Blvd and Georgia backs up post-match
Walk toward Cambie St or Homer St for faster post-match pickup
Pre-book scheduled Uber or Lyft for your return to hotel before the match starts
driving_parking: BC Place and the Plaza of Nations area has limited game-day parking — pre-book strongly advised
Parking at Pacific Centre or Robson Square and walking in is a solid option
Granville Bridge and False Creek routes can grid-lock after full-capacity matches
walking_biking: Downtown Vancouver to BC Place is walkable from most central hotels — 10–20 minutes
Mobi Bike Share has docks throughout Downtown and False Creek
The Seawall path runs from Coal Harbour to False Creek — beautiful pre-match walk
match_day_tips: SkyTrain is genuinely the best option — fast, reliable, and no parking headaches
BC Place roof will be closed or open depending on forecast — confirm closer to match day
Food options in BC Place are good but pricey — eat in Yaletown or Gastown before the match

fan_hubs.name: Plaza of Nations Fan Festival
fan_hubs.description: Right next to BC Place, the Plaza of Nations is the natural hub for tournament fan activity — giant screens, live music, food vendors, and direct waterfront access. One of the best-located fan zones in the tournament.
transport_tips: Walking distance from Yaletown and False Creek North
Arrive 2 hours early for big matches — capacity fills quickly

fan_hubs.name: Granville Island Fan Hub
fan_hubs.description: Granville Island's market and arts complex becomes a natural fan gathering area. International food stalls, outdoor patios with water views, and the relaxed community energy that makes Vancouver unique.
transport_tips: Aquabus ferry from False Creek North to Granville Island — 5 minutes
False Creek Ferries also serve the island from multiple Downtown docks
Public transit bus route 50 from Downtown stops at the island

neighborhoods.name: Downtown / Coal Harbour
neighborhoods.safety_transit_notes: Very safe. Well-lit and pedestrian-heavy along the waterfront.
neighborhoods.stadium_access: 10–15 min walk or SkyTrain from Burrard/Granville to Stadium-Chinatown
neighborhoods.description: The most central location with easy access to BC Place, the Seawall, and Stanley Park. Multiple luxury and business hotel options along the harbour.

neighborhoods.name: Yaletown
neighborhoods.stadium_access: 10-minute walk to BC Place along False Creek
neighborhoods.description: Former warehouse district turned upscale restaurant and bar zone. Some of Vancouver's best restaurants are here, and it's an easy walk to BC Place along the waterfront.

neighborhoods.name: Gastown
neighborhoods.safety_transit_notes: Generally safe in the tourist area. The transition zone east of Gastown toward the DTES requires awareness at night.
neighborhoods.stadium_access: 15–20 min walk or SkyTrain to Stadium-Chinatown
neighborhoods.description: Vancouver's oldest neighbourhood with brick-cobblestone streets, the famous steam clock, and a strong bar and cocktail scene. Excellent for post-match nights.

neighborhoods.name: Kitsilano
neighborhoods.best_for: Beach, outdoor lifestyle, families, longer stays
neighborhoods.stadium_access: 25–35 min by transit via Granville Bridge
neighborhoods.description: A more local neighbourhood feel across False Creek. Kitsilano Beach, great cafés, and a vibrant morning culture. Better for fans staying multiple weeks who want a neighbourhood experience.

hotels.name: The Douglas, Autograph Collection
hotels.best_for: Boutique design, stadium convenience, modern rooms

hotels.name: Fairmont Hotel Vancouver
hotels.best_for: Classic luxury, landmark property, Granville St access

booking_links.label: Browse all Vancouver hotels on Booking.com →

bars.name: Craft Beer Market
bars.notes: One of Vancouver's best sports bars with a massive tap list and multiple screens. Usually packed for big matches.
bars.transit: Walk from BC Place via False Creek

bars.name: The Blarney Stone
bars.notes: Classic Irish pub in Gastown. Reliable soccer showings and a local crowd.

bars.name: Steamworks Brew Pub
bars.notes: Iconic Gastown pub in a converted Victorian building. Screens in multiple areas, good for groups.

bars.name: Twelve West
bars.notes: Rooftop bar on the Granville entertainment strip. Great for an evening out before or after a match.
bars.transit: Bus on Granville, short walk from Downtown

bars.name: The Irish Heather
bars.notes: Vancouver's most acclaimed pub. Whiskey bar attached. Gastown institution with a proper atmosphere.

bars.name: The Roxy
bars.notes: High-energy live music and bar. Long lineups on big match nights — arrive early.

transport.summary: Vancouver has world-class public transit. The SkyTrain drops visitors 2 minutes from BC Place — it's the most convenient stadium access in the tournament. Buy a Compass Card at the airport and use it all week.
tips: Compass Card: tap-to-pay SkyTrain, bus, and SeaBus — buy at YVR or any SkyTrain station
Stadium-Chinatown station on the Expo and Millennium Lines is the BC Place stop
SkyTrain runs every 3–5 minutes during peak hours and extended on match nights
Mobi Bike Share has docks throughout Downtown — great for exploring between matches
Aquabus and False Creek Ferries connect Granville Island and False Creek waterfront to Downtown

fan_zones.name: Plaza of Nations Fan Festival
fan_zones.description: Right next to BC Place with live music, food vendors, giant screens, and waterfront views. Most accessible fan hub in the tournament.

fan_zones.name: Granville Island Fan Hub
fan_zones.description: Arts and market district fan area accessible by ferry across False Creek. International food, outdoor screens, unique Vancouver atmosphere.

soccer_culture.community_notes: Vancouver has a genuine soccer culture built around the Whitecaps, the Canadian national teams, and a diverse diaspora from football-mad countries. BC Place hosted 1994 World Cup matches and the fanbase here is knowledgeable and passionate.
historic_venues: BC Place (1994 World Cup, 2010 Winter Olympics)

tourist_hits.name: Stanley Park
tourist_hits.notes: 1,000-acre urban rainforest with the Seawall, beaches, and totem poles. An absolute must.

tourist_hits.name: Capilano Suspension Bridge
tourist_hits.notes: Popular tourist attraction in North Vancouver. Book tickets in advance — busy in summer.

tourist_hits.name: Granville Island Public Market
tourist_hits.notes: Best local food market in the city. Arrive hungry and leave with provisions.

tourist_hits.name: Gastown Steam Clock
tourist_hits.notes: Historic neighbourhood walk. Gastown has excellent bars and independent shops.

tourist_hits.name: Grouse Mountain
tourist_hits.notes: Gondola ride up for panoramic city views. Disc golf, hiking, and bear habitat.

local_favorites.name: Deep Cove Kayak
local_favorites.notes: Rent kayaks in this stunning North Vancouver inlet. 45-minute drive but worth every minute.

local_favorites.name: Commercial Drive
local_favorites.notes: Multicultural neighbourhood with the best Italian coffee, Ethiopian food, and independent bookshops.

local_favorites.name: Kitsilano Beach
local_favorites.notes: Local's beach — outdoor pool, beach volleyball, the Seawall. Pack a picnic.

local_favorites.name: UBC Museum of Anthropology
local_favorites.notes: World-class collection of Northwest Coast Indigenous art in a stunning building.

areas: Yaletown — upscale restaurants and cocktail bars, 10 min from BC Place
Gastown — historic brick buildings, craft cocktails, late-night options
Robson St — restaurants and shops, tourist-friendly
Commercial Drive — authentic international food, neighbourhood atmosphere
Chinatown — late-night dim sum and Asian food options

recommendations.name: Miku Restaurant
recommendations.notes: Flame-seared aburi sushi in Coal Harbour with harbour views. Book weeks ahead.

recommendations.name: Vij's Restaurant
recommendations.notes: Legendary Indian cuisine on Cambie St. No reservations — lineup is part of the experience.

recommendations.name: Hawksworth Restaurant
recommendations.notes: Fine dining at the Rosewood Hotel Georgia. Best for a special match-night dinner.

local_resources.emergency_info: Emergency: 911. Non-emergency Vancouver Police: (604) 717-3321. Hospital: Vancouver General, 899 W 12th Ave.

walk_bike.walkability_summary: Downtown Vancouver, Yaletown, and Gastown are excellent for walking — flat, well-lit, and compact. The Seawall is one of the world's great urban walks.
walk_bike.bikeability_summary: Vancouver has an excellent network of protected bike lanes. The Seawall is separated from traffic for its entire length.
best_walkable_areas: Seawall from Coal Harbour to Granville Island
walk_bike.bike_share_notes: Mobi Bike Share has docks throughout Downtown, Yaletown, Kitsilano, and the Seawall. Day passes available via the Mobi app or at kiosks.

pickup_soccer.name: Trout Lake Park
pickup_soccer.access_notes: Popular pickup soccer location in East Vancouver. Mixed skill levels and international crowd.

pickup_soccer.name: Callister Park
pickup_soccer.access_notes: Community fields used for informal pickup and youth games. East Vancouver neighbourhood feel.

outdoors_day_trips.name: Whistler
outdoors_day_trips.distance: About 120 km north of Vancouver on Sea-to-Sky Highway
outdoors_day_trips.notes: World-class mountain biking and hiking in summer. The Peak 2 Peak gondola is stunning. The drive itself on Sea-to-Sky Highway is one of the best in North America.

outdoors_day_trips.name: Garibaldi Provincial Park
outdoors_day_trips.notes: Stunning alpine lakes including Garibaldi Lake and Black Tusk. Day hike or overnight. Very popular in July — start early.

outdoors_day_trips.name: Victoria, BC
outdoors_day_trips.distance: BC Ferries from Tsawwassen, about 1.5 hrs
outdoors_day_trips.notes: Beautiful historic city on Vancouver Island. Butchart Gardens, whale watching, and a charming walkable downtown. Great two-day trip.

safety_tips: Vancouver is very safe for tourists in core areas — Downtown, Yaletown, Gastown, and Kitsilano
The Downtown Eastside (DTES) east of Gastown has visible poverty and drug activity — not a tourist area
Keep an eye on belongings on transit and in crowded fan zones
Rideshare is reliable and safe for late-night travel
June can be cool and rainy — always carry a waterproof layer
Wildlife in Stanley Park: do not feed or approach racoons or coyotes
